items.title: The Rain Barrel
items.text: Last summer, the garden at Oakfield Elementary School had a problem. The weather was very dry, and the vegetables began to turn brown. Every morning, the students had to carry heavy buckets of water from the sink. Then Ms. Duran's class had an idea. They asked a neighbor for an old barrel and placed it under the roof gutter, so it filled with rain during storms. Now the students use a small tap on the barrel to water the plants. The work is easier, and the school saves water. The garden is green again.

qs.q: What happened to the vegetables in the dry weather?
qs.why: 본문에 'the vegetables began to turn brown'이라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What can you infer about carrying buckets every morning?
o: It was tiring work for the students.
It was the favorite job of the class.
It took only a minute each day.
It was done by the neighbor.
qs.why: 'heavy buckets'를 매일 아침 날랐다고 했고, 새 방법으로 'The work is easier'가 되었다고 하므로 이전 일은 힘들었다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "tap" means
o: a light touch with a finger
a part that lets water out
a kind of quick dance step
a lid that covers the barrel
qs.why: 통에 달린 'tap'으로 식물에 물을 준다고 했으므로 물이 나오게 하는 작은 장치라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "so it filled with rain during storms," what does "it" refer to?
qs.why: 앞 문장에서 이웃에게 받아 지붕 빗물받이 아래에 놓은 것은 'an old barrel'이고, 그 통이 비로 찼어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why vegetables turn brown in the summer heat
How to build a roof gutter at home
A neighbor who loves growing vegetables
How a class solved a watering problem
qs.why: 물 부족 문제를 빗물 통으로 해결한 학급의 이야기가 글 전체의 중심이에요.

items.title: The Delayed Train
items.text: Hana arrived at the station at 7:50. Her train to her grandmother's town left at 8:00, so she was not worried. But when she looked at the board, the word DELAYED shone next to her train. A worker told the waiting travelers that a tree had fallen across the tracks. Hana felt nervous because her grandmother would be standing outside in the cold. Her phone had no battery, so she borrowed a stranger's phone and sent a short message. Then she sat on a bench and read her book. Forty minutes later, the train finally arrived.

qs.q: What caused the problem with the train?
qs.why: 역 직원이 'a tree had fallen across the tracks'라고 알려 주었어요.

qs.q: Why did Hana most likely send a message?
o: To ask her grandmother to wait inside the station
To tell her grandmother about the delay
To cancel the trip to the town
To ask for a new ticket today
qs.why: 할머니가 추운 바깥에서 기다릴 것을 걱정해 연락했으므로, 기차가 늦는다는 사실을 알리려는 것이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "delayed" means
qs.why: 기차가 8시에 출발해야 하는데 40분 뒤에야 도착했으므로 'delayed'는 예정보다 늦다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "because hers had no battery," what does "hers" refer to?
qs.why: 'hers'는 'her phone'을 줄인 말로, 배터리가 없는 것은 하나의 휴대폰이에요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A girl who dislikes riding trains
How Hana handled a late train
A tree that fell during a storm
Why stations need a big board
qs.why: 기차가 늦어졌을 때 하나가 연락하고 책을 읽으며 대처한 이야기예요.

items.title: Sleep and Growing Bodies
items.text: Doctors say children between six and twelve need nine to twelve hours of sleep each night. While you sleep, your body is busy. It repairs small injuries and makes the hormones that help you grow. Your brain also sorts the things you learned during the day, which is why sleeping before a test can be better than studying all night. Bright screens can make falling asleep harder, so many families turn off phones and tablets an hour before bed. A quiet, dark room helps too. Good sleep is not a waste of time. It is part of staying healthy.

qs.q: How much sleep do children between six and twelve need?
qs.why: 본문에 'nine to twelve hours of sleep each night'이라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What can you infer about a child who sleeps only five hours every night?
o: The child will grow faster than other children.
The child may lack rest for growing and learning.
The child has no need for a quiet, dark room.
The child will remember more things at school.
qs.why: 잠은 몸을 회복시키고 성장 호르몬을 만들며 뇌가 배운 것을 정리하는 시간이므로, 5시간만 자면 부족할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "sorts" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 뇌가 낮에 배운 것을 'sorts'한다는 것은 정리한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "which is why sleeping before a test can be better," what does "which" refer to?
o: the hormones that help you grow
qs.why: 'which'는 앞 절 전체, 즉 뇌가 낮에 배운 것을 정리한다는 사실을 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why did the writer write this passage?
o: To explain why sleep matters for health
To sell screens that help children sleep
To describe a doctor's daily work
To tell a story about a test
qs.why: 잠이 몸과 뇌에 어떤 도움을 주는지 설명하며 건강의 일부라고 마무리해요.

items.title: Tomas the Baker
items.text: Tomas Reyes grew up above his uncle's small bakery in a port town. As a boy, he woke before sunrise to carry flour bags, and he hated it. At sixteen, he wanted to leave and become a sailor. Then one winter morning, a storm stopped the ships, and hungry fishermen filled the shop. Tomas baked bread all day with his uncle. When the last loaf was gone, he felt proud for the first time. He stayed, learned every recipe, and later opened his own shop, where he still teaches young people to bake for free on Saturdays.

qs.q: What did Tomas want to be at sixteen?
qs.why: 본문에 'he wanted to leave and become a sailor'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What most likely changed Tomas's feelings about the bakery?
o: He saw his work help hungry people.
His uncle began to pay him much more money.
The storm destroyed all the ships in the port.
He found an easier job at a different shop.
qs.why: 폭풍 속에서 배고픈 어부들에게 빵을 만들어 준 뒤 처음으로 자랑스러움을 느꼈다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, a "port town" is a town
o: at the top of a mountain
qs.why: 배가 드나들고 선원과 어부가 나오므로 'port town'은 배가 들어오는 항구가 있는 마을이에요.

qs.q: In "where he still teaches young people," what does "where" refer to?
qs.why: 'where'는 바로 앞의 'his own shop'을 가리켜요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Storms are good for the bakery business.
Sailors always make the best bakers.
A boy learns to value baking.
Flour bags are very hard to carry.
qs.why: 빵 만드는 일을 싫어하던 소년이 보람을 느끼고 제빵사가 된 이야기예요.

items.title: Growing a Bean in a Jar
items.text: You can grow a bean plant in a jar. First, fold a paper towel and place it inside a clean glass jar. Next, wet the towel with a little water, but do not make it too wet. Then push two bean seeds between the glass and the towel so you can see them. Put the jar near a window and check it every day. After about a week, small roots will appear. When the roots are as long as your finger, move the bean to a pot with soil. Remember to give it water and sunlight.

qs.q: Where should the jar be placed?
qs.why: 본문에 'Put the jar near a window'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say not to make the towel too wet?
o: Too much water might harm the seeds.
The jar would become too heavy to lift.
qs.why: 'a little water, but do not make it too wet'이라며 물이 너무 많으면 안 된다고 했으므로 씨앗에 해로울 수 있다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "appear" means
qs.why: 약 일주일 뒤 작은 뿌리가 'appear'한다는 것은 눈에 보이게 나타난다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "give it water and sunlight," what does "it" refer to?
qs.why: 뿌리가 자란 콩을 화분으로 옮긴 뒤 물과 햇빛을 주라는 것이므로 'it'은 콩 식물이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the passage?
o: To explain how to grow a bean
To explain why beans taste so good
To tell a story about a garden
To compare jars and clay pots
qs.why: 순서대로 따라 하도록 콩 키우는 방법을 알려 주는 글이에요.

items.title: The Missing Book
items.text: Jun wanted a book about volcanoes for his science project, but the library's only copy was checked out. He felt disappointed and almost went home. Then the librarian, Mr. Cole, showed him a computer. "You can reserve it," he said. Jun typed his name and chose the book. The screen said he was second in line. Four days later, he got a message saying the book was ready. He rushed to the library after school. Although he had less time than his classmates, he finished his project on time.

qs.q: How long did Jun wait for the message?
qs.why: 'Four days later, he got a message'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: Why did Jun most likely rush to the library?
o: The library was about to close for good.
He wanted to meet Mr. Cole again.
He wanted to return another book.
qs.why: 다른 친구들보다 시간이 적었다고 했으므로 프로젝트 때문에 서둘렀다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "checked out" means the book was
o: too old for anyone to read
qs.why: 하나뿐인 책이 'checked out' 상태여서 Jun이 빌릴 수 없었으므로 다른 사람이 빌려 간 상태예요.

qs.q: In ""You can reserve it," he said," who does "he" refer to?
qs.why: 컴퓨터를 보여 준 사람은 사서인 Mr. Cole이고, 그가 예약할 수 있다고 말했어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A boy who is afraid of real volcanoes
A librarian who needs a better computer
How to write a good science report
A student finds a way to get a book
qs.why: 원하는 책이 없던 학생이 예약 제도로 문제를 해결한 이야기예요.

items.title: A New Bike Lane
items.text: Last month, the town of Riverton painted a green bike lane along Mill Street. Before that, many students rode on the sidewalk because the road was crowded with cars. Some walkers complained that bicycles passed too close. Now cyclists have their own space, separated from cars by a row of small posts. The town council says it will watch the lane for six months before building more. So far, a shop owner says more people stop to buy things, because bikes are easy to park outside. Not everyone is happy, though. Some drivers miss the parking spaces that were removed.

qs.q: Why did many students ride on the sidewalk before the bike lane?
o: The road was crowded with cars.
They wanted to race the walkers.
Bicycles were not allowed on the road.
qs.why: 'the road was crowded with cars' 때문에 학생들이 인도로 다녔어요.

qs.q: What can you infer about the town council's plan?
o: It will remove the bike lane next week.
It has already built lanes on every street.
It may build more if the lane works.
It does not care what people think.
qs.why: 6개월 동안 지켜본 뒤 더 만들겠다고 했으므로 결과가 좋으면 확대할 수 있다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "separated" means
qs.why: 작은 기둥들이 자전거를 자동차와 떨어뜨려 놓는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "it will watch the lane for six months," what does "it" refer to?
qs.why: 'The town council says it will watch...'에서 'it'은 주어인 시의회를 가리켜요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention the drivers at the end?
o: To show a downside of the change
To prove that the lane has failed
To advertise a parking lot downtown
To describe how fast cars can drive
qs.why: 'Not everyone is happy'라며 주차 공간이 없어진 불만을 소개해 변화의 다른 면을 보여 줘요.

items.title: Nora at the Clinic
items.text: Nora did not like the clinic. The smell was strong, and the waiting room was cold. Today she needed a vaccine shot, and her hands were shaking. The nurse, Ms. Patel, did not hurry. She asked Nora to name her favorite animal. "Elephants," Nora answered, and they talked about how elephants use their trunks like hands. Before Nora noticed, the shot was finished. "That's all?" she asked. The nurse laughed and gave her a sticker shaped like an elephant. Nora walked out surprised that something so scary had been so quick.

qs.q: What did the nurse ask Nora to do?
o: Draw a picture of an elephant
qs.why: 'She asked Nora to name her favorite animal.'이라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: Why did the nurse most likely talk about elephants?
o: To teach her facts about animals
To show she had seen elephants
To finish the work more quickly
To take her mind off the shot
qs.why: 코끼리 이야기를 하는 동안 주사가 끝났으므로, 간호사는 Nora의 관심을 다른 곳으로 돌려 긴장을 풀어 주려 한 것이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "noticed" means
qs.why: 'Before Nora noticed'는 Nora가 알아차리기도 전에 주사가 끝났다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In ""That's all?" she asked," what does "That" refer to?
qs.why: 주사가 끝난 것을 모르고 있던 Nora가 이것이 전부냐고 묻는 것이므로 'That'은 주사예요.

qs.q: How did Nora's feeling change in the story?
qs.why: 처음엔 손이 떨릴 만큼 무서워했지만 끝나고는 너무 빨라서 놀랐어요.

items.title: Penguins in the Wind
items.text: In Antarctica, winter winds can be colder than a freezer. To stay alive, emperor penguins stand very close together in a huge group called a huddle. The penguins on the outside face the strongest wind, so they cannot stay there forever. Slowly, the group moves, and each bird takes a turn in the warm middle. Scientists say that this shuffle lets almost every penguin share the cold equally. Inside the huddle, the temperature can be much higher than outside. Without teamwork, the penguins could not survive the long, dark winter.

qs.q: Which penguins face the strongest wind?
qs.why: 'The penguins on the outside face the strongest wind'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What does the moving of the huddle show about the penguins?
o: They are afraid of the scientists.
They like to travel very far.
qs.why: 모두가 차례로 따뜻한 가운데에 들어간다고 했으므로 서로 협력함을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "shuffle" means
o: a loud call to the group
a kind of food for chicks
qs.why: 무리가 천천히 움직이며 새들이 자리를 바꾸는 것을 'shuffle'이라고 했어요.

qs.q: In "they cannot stay there forever," what does "there" refer to?
qs.why: 바람을 가장 많이 맞는 바깥쪽에 계속 있을 수 없다는 뜻이므로 'there'는 무리의 바깥쪽이에요.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Penguins can fly to warmer places each year.
Antarctica is colder than any freezer.
Scientists often study penguins in freezers.
qs.why: 황제펭귄이 서로 모여 번갈아 자리를 바꾸며 겨울을 견딘다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

items.title: Amara and the Water Filter
items.text: Dr. Amara Okoye grew up in a village where the well water was often dirty. Her classmates missed school because they were sick. At fourteen, she began testing sand, stones, and charcoal in plastic bottles to find a cheap way to clean water. Many of her first filters failed, but she kept notes on each mistake. After years of study, she designed a filter that cost less than a school lunch. Today, her design is used in many villages, and she tells students that every failure teaches something.

qs.q: What did Amara test in plastic bottles?
qs.why: 'testing sand, stones, and charcoal in plastic bottles'라고 나와 있어요.

qs.q: What can you infer about Amara's character?
o: She gives up when work is hard.
She never makes a single mistake.
qs.why: 많은 필터가 실패했어도 실수를 기록하며 계속했으므로 끈기 있고 실패에서 배우는 사람이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "designed" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 여러 해 연구 끝에 필터를 계획하고 만들어 냈다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "because they were sick," who does "they" refer to?
qs.why: 학교에 결석한 것은 'Her classmates'이고, 그들이 아팠어요.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to find a cheap school lunch
A village that has no school at all
How a girl solved a water problem
A scientist who hates plastic bottles
qs.why: 더러운 물 문제를 해결하려던 아이가 유용한 정수 필터를 만든 이야기예요.

items.title: The Frozen Screen
items.text: On Monday, Mr. Lee's art class met online. Just as Pablo started to show his drawing, his screen froze. His face stayed still with his mouth open, and the other students began to laugh. Pablo could hear them, but he could not move. He turned his camera off and on again. Nothing changed. Then he remembered his sister's advice: close other programs first. After he closed three games, the video worked again. "Sorry, everyone," he said. Mr. Lee smiled and said that everybody has a frozen moment sometime. Pablo laughed too and finally shared his drawing.

qs.q: What fixed Pablo's problem?
qs.why: 카메라를 껐다 켜도 소용없었고, 게임 세 개를 닫은 뒤에야 영상이 다시 작동했어요.

qs.q: How did Pablo probably feel when the students laughed?
qs.why: 화면이 멈춘 우스운 얼굴을 친구들이 보고 웃었으므로 쑥스러웠을 거예요.

qs.q: In the passage, "froze" means
qs.why: 화면 속 얼굴이 가만히 멈춰 있었다고 했으므로 'froze'는 멈췄다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "Pablo could hear them," who does "them" refer to?
qs.why: 웃고 있던 'the other students'의 소리를 들을 수 있었어요.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Lee say that everybody has a frozen moment?
o: To blame Pablo for the problem
To teach a lesson about games
qs.why: 누구에게나 있는 일이라는 말로 당황한 Pablo를 안심시키려는 것이에요.

items.title: Lakeside Pool Visitor Guide
items.text: Welcome to Lakeside Pool! Please read these steps before you swim. First, take a quick shower and put your bag in a locker. Children under ten must swim with an adult within arm's reach. Walk, don't run, near the water because the floor is slippery. If you hear one long whistle, leave the pool and wait on the benches. It means the lifeguards need to check the water. The pool closes at six o'clock, but the last swim begins at a quarter to six. Please return your locker key at the desk before you go home.

qs.q: When does the last swim begin?
qs.why: 'a quarter to six'는 5시 45분이에요.

qs.q: Why does the guide most likely ask visitors to shower first?
o: To help warm up the lockers
To get a key for the bag
qs.why: 수영 전 샤워는 몸을 씻어 수영장 물을 깨끗하게 유지하려는 것으로 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, the word "slippery" means
qs.why: 물가 바닥에서 뛰지 말라고 한 이유이므로 미끄러지기 쉽다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In "It means the lifeguards need to check the water," what does "It" refer to?
o: the closing time of the pool
qs.why: 긴 호루라기 소리가 들리면 물에서 나와 기다리라고 했고, 그 소리의 의미를 설명하는 문장이에요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this passage?
o: To tell a story about a swimmer
To describe the history of the pool
To compare pools in different towns
qs.why: 수영장 이용자가 따라야 할 규칙과 순서를 안내하는 글이에요.
